summary: Final MV-2015-240 readout of rat Oral/IV PK with tandem-MS bioanalysis. Systemic clearance was acceptable but oral exposure remained limited, leading Aldrevessa to revisit the dosing vehicle; the displayed PK subset is distinguished from the wider test article set.

slides.title: Study scope and displayed subset
bullets: {{PRJ0057:n_compounds}} test articles in the project record; {{PRJ0057:lims_id}}
The supplied PK table covers the measured subset, not the entire accession lot
slides.notes: The project count is not an animal count or a claim that every test article has a PK row.

slides.title: Rat matrix and route comparison
bullets: Rat plasma parent-analyte measurements by tandem-MS bioanalysis
Protocol: 1 mg/kg IV and 5 mg/kg PO; n=3
Use dose-normalized route exposure for bioavailability; IV clearance describes systemic disposition
slides.notes: Route comparison assumes comparable assay performance and sufficiently linear disposition over the dose range. Individual concentration-time profiles are held in the bioanalytical data package; this deck shows derived parameters only.

slides.title: Matrix acceptance comes first
bullets: Helen Marchwood: review rat-plasma matrix acceptance for reporting sequences
Javier Quintana: inspect calibration, extracted controls and carryover for each analyte
A plausible PK profile does not establish satisfactory analytical performance

slides.title: Analytical and sampling limits
bullets: Terminal estimates require quantifiable late samples and an identifiable elimination interval
Do not replace below-quantitation observations with invented concentrations
AUC, Cmax, sampling times and compound-specific quantitation limits are not supplied
slides.notes: Exposure is conventionally expressed in ng·h/mL. No numerical AUC or concentration-time profile is reconstructed from clearance and bioavailability.

slides.title: Systemic disposition: IV clearance
slides.notes: Complete referenced test article set, in assay worksheet order; this is not a sorted ranking.

slides.title: Route comparison: oral bioavailability
slides.notes: Complete referenced test article set, in assay worksheet order; this is not a sorted ranking.

slides.title: AT15 sulfonyl piperazines
slides.notes: Representative structures aid identity matching; they do not designate nominated leads.

slides.title: Read the routes together
bullets: Acceptable systemic clearance does not establish satisfactory absorption
The recorded project interpretation was limited oral exposure despite acceptable systemic clearance
Bioavailability varies across the displayed subset; the vehicle decision does not mean uniformly poor F
slides.notes: The interpretation concerns the project exposure gate, not a common mechanism assigned to every analogue.

slides.title: Decision: revisit the dosing vehicle
bullets: Aldrevessa Therapeutics returned to the vehicle before the next oral exposure assessment
Review delivery, dispersion and dose preparation alongside the parent-analyte record
Preserve a suitable IV reference in the repeat comparison to separate formulation from disposition

slides.title: Final handoff
bullets: Megan Larkin: retain route assumptions in the DMPK memo
Javier Quintana: keep analytical limits with the analyte cards
Archive the current summary under {{PRJ0057:lims_id}}; vehicle follow-up is a subsequent study
